ao.title: Arctic Oscillation: is cold air escaping?
ao.detail: Model average goes as low as -0.7 (Nov 6) and as high as +0.1. Below -2 = cold air can escape south. Above +2.5 = cold stays up north.

nao.title: North Atlantic Oscillation: is cold air steered our way?
nao.detail: Model average goes as low as -0.7 (Nov 13) and as high as +0.5. Below -1.5 = cold air gets steered into the East.

erie.title: Lake Erie water temperature

vortex.title: Will the polar vortex break down?
vortex.detail: In 31 of 31 runs of the American weather model, the spinning winds over the Arctic stop and reverse within 16 days, as early as Nov 5. That can send Arctic air south 1 to 3 weeks later. Yesterday: 100%.

noreaster.detail: 6 of 31 model runs show a strong storm off the Northeast coast around Nov 13. Strongest run: 972 mb (lower = stronger).

freeze.title: First freeze in Buffalo

lakeeffect.title: Lake-effect snow setup?

recent.text: 🌫️ Sea smoke photo morning. When air about 30°F colder than the lake sits over it, the lake "steams" like a hot bath, making wisps of fog called sea smoke. Lake Erie is 61°F and 20 of 31 model runs (65%) drop Buffalo to 31°F or colder around Nov 13. Best right at sunrise with light wind.

🧊 First freeze coming to Buffalo. Buffalo hasn't dropped to 32°F yet this fall. In 17 of 31 runs of the American weather model (55%), it freezes around Nov 12. The first freeze ends the growing season: frost kills off gardens and tender plants.

🌊 Lake Erie is at a new record warm for Nov 2: 61.0°F, about 6°F warmer than normal. The record for this date is 59.8°F (2024). Warm lake water is fuel for lake-effect snow: when cold air blows over it, the lake adds heat and moisture, which can build heavier snow bands.

❄️ Lake-effect snow setup. When cold air flows over the warmer lake, the lake heats and moistens it, and it rises into snow bands. Forecasters look for the lake to be about 23°F (13°C) warmer than the air 5,000 feet up, with that air cold enough for snow. In 14 of 31 runs of the American weather model (45%), that happens over Lake Erie around Nov 11. Wind direction decides who gets buried.

🌀 Nor'easter signal. A nor'easter is a strong storm that spins up off the East Coast and pulls in wind, rain and snow from the northeast. In 12 of 31 runs of the American weather model (39%), a powerful storm (pressure below 990 mb) forms off New England around Nov 10. Lower pressure means a stronger storm; the strongest run drops to 968 mb.

🌪️ The polar vortex may break down. The polar vortex is a huge spinning wind high above the Arctic that usually keeps the coldest air locked up north. In 29 of 31 runs of the American weather model (94%), that spin stops and reverses, as early as Nov 4. When that happens, Arctic air often spills south 1 to 3 weeks later, which can mean cold and snow for Buffalo. Yesterday it was 71%.

🗺️ NOAA's forecast for Nov 3–Nov 7 got more confident: Buffalo now has a 70% chance of being warmer than normal (before: 60% chance warmer than normal). This comes from NOAA's Climate Prediction Center, which forecasts whether the weeks ahead will run warmer or colder than usual.

🌊 Lake Erie is unusually warm for Oct 26: 61.9°F, about 4°F warmer than normal. The record for this date is 62.1°F (2017). Warm lake water is fuel for lake-effect snow: when cold air blows over it, the lake adds heat and moisture, which can build heavier snow bands.

In 20 of 31 runs of the American weather model (65%), that spin stops and reverses, as early as Nov 4. When that happens, Arctic air often spills south 1 to 3 weeks later, which can mean cold and snow for Buffalo. Yesterday it was 35%.
